NDT training near Hobbs: Lea County college options, Permian inspection employers and online study compared

Hobbs sits in the middle of steady Permian Basin inspection work, yet local NDT schooling is thin. New Mexico Junior College teaches welding, and its catalogue includes destructive testing and a codes course, but our review found no NDT method course there. The nearest dedicated NDT degree we verified is at Amarillo College in the Texas Panhandle. Most Hobbs technicians therefore get into the trade through an inspection company, or study the theory online and complete the practical with an employer.

Who offers NDT training around Hobbs?

  • New Mexico Junior College, Hobbs. NMJC's welding AAS and certificate are built around AWS entry-level welder skill standards. They include a Destructive Testing course (guided bend, tension, impact and nick-break tests) and an Industrial Codes and Standards course covering API, ASME and AWS D1.1. That gives useful context for weld inspection; it is not NDT method training, and the college's workforce catalogue lists no NDT or radiation safety course.
  • Amarillo College. Its Nondestructive Testing and Evaluation programme offers an associate degree and certificates covering visual, magnetic particle, penetrant, radiographic, ultrasonic and eddy current testing, with evening classes available and fall or spring starts. Amarillo is a long drive north of Lea County, so for most Hobbs residents this is a relocation decision.
  • Permian inspection employers. Companies serving production, gathering and processing sites hire assistants and Level II technicians. A Hobbs-based Level II field technician posting from Precision NDT asked for Level II in ultrasonic, magnetic particle and penetrant testing, experience in oil and gas work, and the ability to travel between job sites. Assistants at firms like this usually start by preparing surfaces, carrying equipment and helping technicians while their hours are logged toward Level I.
  • The Texas side of the basin. For candidates willing to work across the state line, see Odessa, Midland and the Permian Basin page.

Which Hobbs route fits you?

Where you standRoute that suits Lea CountyFind out beforehand
No NDT job yetAn assistant role with a Permian inspection company, or relocation for a college programmeWhether the company logs your training and on-the-job hours
Welder from NMJC or the fieldAdd VT and MT, then UTWhether you also want the AWS CWI for weld inspection roles
Level I or II needing UT, MT or PT Level IIOnline theory plus a practical with your employerThat your hours by method match the written practice
Inspection contractor certifying field crewsTraining and Level III examinations at your own yardRecords that an operator's contractor audit will accept

Destructive testing or NDT: know which one you are training for. The destructive tests taught in NMJC's welding programme cut, bend, pull or break a sample to prove a weld procedure or a welder's skill, and the sample is scrap afterwards. NDT examines the actual weld, pipe or vessel without harming it, which is why operators can test equipment that stays in service. Both matter in the Permian: destructive tests qualify welders and procedures before work starts, while NDT checks production welds and tracks corrosion for years afterwards. A welder who already understands why a bend test fails has a head start on interpreting MT and UT indications, so the two kinds of training fit together well. If you want a gauge of how much NDT theory you already know, try the free Level II practice tests.

Questions for any NDT trainer serving Hobbs

  • Are the practice specimens field-realistic, such as pitted pipe, girth welds and threaded connections, or only flat plates?
  • How many hours does the course give for UT, and do they meet the SNT-TC-1A recommendation for the level you want?
  • Who signs your certification? It is an employer under its written practice, or ASNT after its central exams; no course does it by itself.
  • Can you ask a Level III technical questions while you study, and through what channel?
  • If you want radiography work later, will the employer arrange the radiation safety training separately?

Where Atlantis fits for Hobbs candidates and employers

Atlantis has no training location in Lea County. You study each method's theory online at your own pace, starting on the day you enrol, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions. Then you rehearse in the Practical NDT simulator and do the hands-on practical and its examination at your employer's shop or field site, under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, before the employer certifies you. The methods Hobbs postings name are covered in ultrasonic testing training, magnetic particle testing training and penetrant testing training; begin at NDT Level 1 if you are new.

This route works well for someone already employed by an inspection company or an operator, because the practical needs an employer's equipment and written practice. Contractors can have training delivered on site and ask for a quote. Weld-inspection roles in the basin often want a CWI as well; the six-day AWS CWI exam preparation course covers that, with AWS running the exam. See also NDT training in New Mexico.
